title: Mustard-glazed Christmas ham
summary: A fully cooked ham warmed through slowly, then brushed with a mustard, egg-yolk and allulose glaze and browned, in the manner of the Swedish julskinka.

ingredients.note: one 4.5 kg (10 lb) bone-in, fully cooked ham, skin removed; about 3.6 kg is meat. Choose one cured without honey or added sugar where possible

steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F). Set the ham fat side up in a roasting pan, add the water and bay leaves and cover the pan tightly with foil.
Bake until a thermometer in the thickest part (not touching the bone) reads 55 °C (130 °F), about 15 minutes per 450 g (1 lb), roughly 2¼ hours.
Meanwhile whisk the mustard, mustard powder, egg yolk, allulose, cloves and pepper into a smooth glaze.
Take the ham out and raise the oven to 200 °C (400 °F). Score the fat in a diamond pattern, brush the glaze thickly over the top and sides and, if using, pat on the almond flour.

Return the ham uncovered for 15–20 minutes, until the glaze is set and browned and the centre reads 60 °C (140 °F). Allulose browns quickly, so check after 10 minutes and tent with foil if it darkens too fast.
Rest 20 minutes, then slice. Serve warm, or chill and slice thin for the cold table.
tips: A ham labelled 'cook before eating' instead of 'fully cooked' must reach 63 °C (145 °F) and rest 3 minutes.
Studding the fat with whole cloves is an English and American touch; the Swedish coat is mustard, egg and crumbs.

origin.history: Ham has been the centrepiece of the Swedish Christmas table, the julbord, for well over a century. The cured ham is cooked, then brushed with mustard, egg and breadcrumbs and browned in the oven, a step called griljering. Glazed Christmas hams are also traditional in England and across the rest of Scandinavia.
